live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a Rust ransomware-as-a-service gang known for leak-site extortion and a 2024 exit scam
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, ran a Rust-based ransomware-as-a-service operation from November 2021. It hit hospitals, cities and big firms, was disrupted by the FBI in December 2023, and appeared to exit-scam in March 2024.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also known as ALPHVM, BlackCat, Noberus, Ambitious Scorpius and UNC4466.
Malpedia says ALPHV has been seen in ransomware attacks since November 18, 2021.
It is a ransomware-as-a-service operation. Affiliates carry out attacks using the core group's malware.
Several reports say ALPHV is believed to be a rebrand of the DarkSide and BlackMatter operations.
Cisco Talos describes the links between BlackMatter and BlackCat as probable. It has moderate confidence that BlackMatter affiliates were among BlackCat's early adopters.
A BlackCat representative told Recorded Future that the two groups were connected but that BlackCat was not a rebranding of BlackMatter.
eSentire reports that various security teams say the core operators are based in Russia. The report does not verify this itself.
Mandiant tracks the ALPHV operator as UNC3507.
The FBI linked the group to over 60 breaches worldwide in its first four months, from November 2021 to March 2022.
BleepingComputer reports an FBI estimate of at least $300 million in ransom payments from more than 1,000 victims up to September 2023.
Victims named in reports include Henry Schein, a dental and medical distributor, and Constellation Software, a Canadian software group.
They also include the city of Alexandria, Louisiana, and Suffolk County, New York, where the attack disabled the 911 system.
Recorded Future News says Black Cat/AlphV has made a point of going after healthcare and pharmaceutical companies. Sun Pharmaceuticals listed on its leak site on March 24 is one example.
The gang claimed breaches of loanDepot and Prudential Financial. These were its own claims, and it had not yet published proof.
The malware is written in Rust. It runs on Windows, Linux and VMware ESXi.
It can be set to encrypt files with AES or ChaCha20. It can delete volume shadow copies, stop services and ESXi virtual machines, and spread with PsExec.
Symantec reports updates in 2022 that added an ARM build, safe-mode encryption and searchable leak sites. It also saw the Exmatter exfiltration tool used alongside the ransomware.
Symantec saw an affiliate use the Eamfo infostealer to go after credentials stored in Veeam backups.
The gang steals data and threatens to publish it on a leak site. In one case it also threatened to spam the victim's customers.
Sygnia investigated a 2023 case it attributed to BlackCat or one of its affiliates. Access came through a compromised third-party vendor.
In that case the attacker used Cobalt Strike and tunnelling tools, then copied data out with Rclone to cloud storage.
eSentire says Russian-speaking affiliates used Google ads to push the Nitrogen initial-access malware, which led to ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware.
In a statement relayed by one outlet, AlphV said it had launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors at MGM Resorts on September 11, 2023. These are AlphV's own unverified claims.
In December 2023, an international law enforcement operation seized the gang's Tor negotiation and leak sites.
In December 2023, DataBreaches reported that AlphV claimed to have pushed a Viking Therapeutics employee to file an SEC complaint. The claim was unconfirmed.
In February 2024, unnamed sources linked the Change Healthcare attack to BlackCat. BleepingComputer could not confirm this, and UnitedHealth's SEC filing described a suspected nation-state actor.
In March 2024, BleepingComputer reported that the gang appeared to be running an exit scam. Its sites went offline, affiliates said they were not paid, and it offered its source code for $5 million.
The gang posted a fake FBI seizure banner. Europol and the NCA said they were not involved in any recent disruption.
The Malpedia page lists a US Justice Department release dated 2025-12-30 saying two Americans pleaded guilty to targeting US victims with ALPHV BlackCat ransomware.
Patch internet-facing systems, protect backup credentials and watch for abuse of remote access tools.
